Peri-implant mucositis

One trial found improved plaque, bleeding, probing-depth, and pain measures when broad-spectrum light was added to debridement, while another found no added effect on its measured clinical indices.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One trial found improved plaque, bleeding, probing-depth, and pain measures when broad-spectrum light was added to debridement, while another found no added effect on its measured clinical indices.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact database subcategory contains five human titles. Two randomized trials directly study peri-implant mucositis. Two additional randomized trials concern peri-implantitis, and one small self-controlled report concerns implant overdentures; those neighboring conditions are not direct mucositis evidence. No animal or in-vitro study was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

In a 40-person randomized trial, broad polarized polychromatic light was added to professional mechanical debridement. The authors reported improvements in plaque, probing depth, bleeding, and pain compared with debridement alone (Nardi et al. 2022). A separate 34-person randomized trial tested a single 940-nm diode-laser session after debridement. It found no significant between-group effect on modified plaque or gingival indices, probing depth, peri-implant sulcular-fluid volume, or cortisol (Alhumaidan et al. 2022). The two trials therefore do not show a consistent effect across devices and outcomes.

Animal evidence

No relevant animal study was found in the exact mucositis category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone laboratory or ex-vivo record was identified in this category.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The positive trial used a Bioptron source spanning 480–3400 nm, with reported irradiance of 40 mW/cm² and fluence of 2.4 J/cm², across eight sessions in four weeks. The null trial used a 940-nm near-infrared diode laser in one session after debridement. These approaches differ in spectrum and schedule, and both were adjuncts to mechanical care rather than isolated treatments.

Interpretation

The direct evidence is limited to two small, dissimilar trials with conflicting results. The additional peri-implantitis and overdenture records can inform context but should not be counted as independent evidence for mucositis.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term plaque, bleeding, and probing measures because two direct randomized trials report conflicting results
Publications and records5 unique titles in the database subcategory

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Only two randomized trials directly address peri-implant mucositis, and they use different light sources and schedules. One found added improvements in selected clinical measures while the other found no between-group effect on the reported indices. More independent trials using standardized diagnosis, debridement, and follow-up are needed.
